When you work construction, you don't stop. You have a schedule. You do everything to keep on schedule including working around the clock. People get hurt and people die, but the job must continue. If you don't drive the piles today, in sixteen months, someone has to pay extra money for changing the contract of the roofing company. Most people don't understand this.

That said....... Working a GIANT job.... For an unnamed multi-billionaire developer in flashy tourist gambling town somewhere in America, there was an accident. 5 top people killed one morning in a corporate jet crash. Shock throughout the family....the construction family. Because the multi-billionaire developer hires and works with those people that become as close as family, even if they've never met before the job started. They have a bond. They become like family soon after starting a GIANT project. It's a beautiful thing to witness. The way people work together.

The multi-billionaire was shaken to his core. It could have been him on that jet. The rest of his team, everyone....from the senior vice president down to the laborer foreman, kept working. Everyone went to the wakes after work.... some of them in shirt sleeves and some of them in dirty work clothes. They juggled their own work schedules to attend the funerals in the mornings that followed. The job continued. There was a brief pause that last morning, ...4 days after the plane crash. The job site shut down. More than two thousand workers in different colored hardhats stopped what they were doing and gathered together where concrete mixers were bleating in reverse, deep tracks of bulldozers cut through the raw dirt and huge piles of earth lined the construction site. The concrete mixers stopped bleating as they stopped moving, but they never stopped turning at idle.

A priest walked to the front of a crowd of family. He shook hands with the mayor.

There had to be a hundred of them. The family members, I mean. With kids and old people. You could tell they were the family because they were the only people not wearing hardhats.

They grimaced as gusts of wind blew raw dirt and grit into their faces and whipped the flag.

The priest gathered attention and started to read passages from the Bible.

As he was reading, I looked back at the job. They were just 10 or 12 levels above grade... 35 more to go. ...the cores of the buildings they would soon be.

And as I watched, I saw the tower cranes turning towards the family gathering. All six of them. Like tall soldiers moving in slow unison.

They all stopped, pointing directly at the flag flying at half mast at the main entrance behind the priest. The priest finished reading from the Bible and made the sign of the cross.

In the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit... Amen.

Then one by one, the tower cranes started to wail.
The Saddest Thing I Ever Saw on a Job Site Was the Wailing of the Tower Cranes.
